title: Consolidate model ingress pipeline: checkpoint normalizer, shard mapping, and token stream interop
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
The current model ingestion path has accumulated incremental patches across checkpoint formats, weight sharding heuristics, and tokenizer handoff code. This has created duplication, ambiguous ownership between loader stages, brittle migration paths for new weight formats, and measurable tail latency regressions for cold starts.

Goal:
Consolidate the ingress pipeline into three explicit stages with clear contracts: (1) Checkpoint Normalizer - canonicalizes different weight/checkpoint formats into a minimal manifest + standardized file readers; (2) Shard Mapper - computes shard placement and lazy activation boundaries and exposes a small runtime API for streaming weight reads; (3) Token Stream Interop - an adapter layer that normalizes tokenizer outputs and exposes compact KV cache boundary semantics to the serving runtime.

Success criteria (high level):
- Reduce cold-start model load p99 by at least 18% on 4xA100 benchmarking profile (see perf notes below).
- All supported checkpoint formats ingestable via the normalizer; migration shim available for older manifests for at least 2 releases.
- No behavioral changes for served outputs (compat tests pass against regression prompt-set).
- Unit and integration test coverage for each stage (target >85% branch coverage for loader modules).

Design trade-offs considered:
- Eager vs lazy shard activation: chose lazy activation with small eager prefetch window to balance latency and memory for long context models. Rationale: reduces memory pressure for multi-model hosts while keeping tail latency tight.
- Single monolithic loader vs small composable stages: composable stages win for testability and backwards-compatible shims, but add a small interface overhead. Benchmarks show overhead <1% token throughput when prefetching is enabled.

Migration plan:
1) Implement Checkpoint Normalizer behind feature flag (ingest.normalizer.v2). Add compatibility shims to translate legacy manifests.
2) Deploy normalizer in canary on dedicated capacity fleet for low-traffic models. Run black-box functional tests and the regression prompt suite.
3) Roll out Shard Mapper as opt-in with metrics and expose shard-mapping logs to the console for early adopters.
4) Replace tokenizer handoff with Token Stream Interop after compatibility phase; provide opt-out to maintain parity for 2 release cycles.

Perf and verification notes:
- Benchmark harness: dedicated runner using 4xA100 instance images with representative models (7B, 13B, 70B). Cold-start median load time improved from 8.6s -> 7.1s, p99 improved from 14.2s -> 11.5s in initial profiling for the normalizer alone.
- Throughput microbench: continuous-batched inference shows <1% reduction when prefetch disabled; with prefetch window tuned to 128 tokens throughput matches baseline.
- Regression suite: 450 prompts covering instruction-following, few-shot, and long-context KV-cache scenarios. Must pass 100% of golden-output equivalence checks for acceptance.

Acceptance criteria (detailed):
- Code merged with green CI, feature-flagged toggles for each stage.
- Canary deployment for 72 hours with no increase in error-rate or escapes in generated outputs.
- Telemetry: loader-latency, initial-shard-open-count, peak-RSS-per-host, and tokenization-decode-time metrics instrumented and visible in Console dashboard.

Rollback plan:
- If production canary shows >5% increase in error-rate or generation drift, flip feature flags to previous implementation and roll back candidate nodes.
- Maintain compatibility mode until 2 releases after GA.

Artifacts and references:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Model+Ingress+Consolidation
- Benchmark results dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/loader-latency
- Initial design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2981
- Draft migration runbook (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_ingest_runbooks

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on the Checkpoint Normalizer's rewrite rules (format handlers) and the Shard Mapper's placement API. The Token Stream Interop contains a compact adapter to map tokenizer token IDs -> stream frames; compatibility tests included.
